title: AFTER UPDATE Triggers and OLD/NEW Values
learningObjectives: Explain the difference between OLD and NEW in an UPDATE trigger.
Create an AFTER UPDATE OF column trigger.
Use a WHEN condition to record only meaningful changes.
Capture old and new values in an audit table.
Explain how update auditing supports traceability.

understand.concept: An UPDATE trigger can inspect OLD values before the change and NEW values after the change. An AFTER UPDATE trigger is useful for recording what changed after a row update succeeds.
understand.whyItMatters: Auditing updates helps explain changes to important fields such as prices, statuses and account settings.
understand.analogy: A trigger is like an automatic rule attached to a data event: it runs when the specified change occurs, even if the application did not call it directly.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not model OLD/NEW row values, transaction timing, recursive execution or DBMS-specific trigger semantics.

explain.narrative:
## OLD and NEW
In an UPDATE trigger, OLD refers to the row values before the update and NEW refers to the values after the update. A trigger can compare them or store both in an audit table.

## AFTER UPDATE OF column
SQLite allows an UPDATE OF column_name trigger clause to fire when the named column appears in the SET list. A WHEN condition can further restrict which row changes are logged.

## Avoid unnecessary audit noise
Use a WHEN condition such as OLD.price IS NOT NEW.price to avoid recording updates where the value did not actually change. Audit tables should record the minimum information required by the business and retention policy.

examples.title: Create a product table
examples.code: CREATE TABLE trg17_products (product_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, product_name TEXT NOT NULL, price INTEGER NOT NULL);
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates create a product table using SQLite triggers. Verify the event, timing and affected rows.

examples.title: Create a price audit table
examples.code: CREATE TABLE trg17_price_audit (audit_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, product_id INTEGER NOT NULL, old_price INTEGER NOT NULL, new_price INTEGER NOT NULL);
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates create a price audit table using SQLite triggers. Verify the event, timing and affected rows.

examples.title: Insert a starting product
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates insert a starting product using SQLite triggers. Verify the event, timing and affected rows.

examples.title: Create an AFTER UPDATE trigger
examples.code: CREATE TRIGGER trg17_price_update AFTER UPDATE OF price ON trg17_products WHEN OLD.price IS NOT NEW.price BEGIN INSERT INTO trg17_price_audit(product_id, old_price, new_price) VALUES (OLD.product_id, OLD.price, NEW.price); END;
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates create an after update trigger using SQLite triggers. Verify the event, timing and affected rows.

examples.title: Update the price and inspect the audit
examples.code: UPDATE trg17_products SET price = 55 WHERE product_id = 1; SELECT product_id, old_price, new_price FROM trg17_price_audit;
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates update the price and inspect the audit using SQLite triggers. Verify the event, timing and affected rows.

practise.guidedTask: Run the examples and identify the old and new price captured by the trigger.
practise.independentTask: Create an employee table and an AFTER UPDATE trigger that records changes to department_id, including the old and new department values.
hints: OLD contains values before the update.
NEW contains values after the update.
UPDATE OF column limits which SET columns activate the trigger.
Use WHEN OLD.column IS NOT NEW.column to avoid no-op audit rows.
Store only the fields required for audit and retention.

questions.prompt: What does OLD represent in an UPDATE trigger?
options: The row values before the update
The row values after the update
The database schema
The next row
questions.answer: The row values before the update

questions.prompt: What does NEW represent in an UPDATE trigger?
options: The row values after the update
The old table definition
The prior database backup
The last deleted row
questions.answer: The row values after the update

questions.prompt: What does UPDATE OF price specify?
options: The trigger responds when price appears in the UPDATE SET list
The trigger creates a price column
The trigger runs on every SELECT
The trigger drops the price index
questions.answer: The trigger responds when price appears in the UPDATE SET list
questions.explanation: UPDATE OF names the columns whose updates activate the trigger.

questions.prompt: Why use a WHEN OLD.price IS NOT NEW.price condition?
options: To avoid logging an update when the value did not actually change
To force every update to fail
To delete the audit table
To make price a primary key
questions.answer: To avoid logging an update when the value did not actually change
questions.explanation: The WHEN condition filters out unchanged values.

questions.prompt: What is a common use for an AFTER UPDATE trigger?
options: Record old and new values for an audit trail
Replace all SELECT queries
Create a database user
Disable constraints
questions.answer: Record old and new values for an audit trail
questions.explanation: An AFTER UPDATE trigger can record a successful change.
